     - `bounds`: the virtual node's snapshot bounds.

     - `shifts`: the canvas's, their holders named by stable id.

# Forks — 2026-11-25-virtual-nodes-in-every-read («Virtual nodes in every read», v040-11)

Written at phase P4, before any plan, on the operator's directive (`inputs#I1`). No default is taken: every fork waits
for its word. The phase run dir is `.andromeda/runs/2026-11-25T10-53-07-phase/`. Each «measured» figure below says how
it was read. No runtime cost was measured: no probe ran and no worktree was made.

The fork numbers go on from «Virtual nodes as elements» (F7–F12,
`chunks/2026-11-25-virtual-nodes-as-elements/evidence/founder-forks.md`). The new forks are F13–F22.

**Whose it is** (the same rule as the last two chunks):
- **Founder's**: the entry, a CARRY or a standing rule names his word; an option amends a row ratified on his own word;
  or an option changes engine behaviour for every document with no ruling (learning 2026-10-18).
- **Operator's**: a consequence inside rulings he already gave — closed words, booleans and numbers inside a ratified
  carrier (`decision/closed-value-field-no-widening`).
- Unclear: the fork says so, and the operator routes it.

**Founder's forks found: one certain (F13), and one more only on one option each (F15 B, F16 D, F19 C).** F13 is
also open to the operator's reading of F3 A; it says so below.

## Measured facts the forks rest on
- **M1 — the graph excepts virtual nodes in one filter.** `DioxusDocument::graph` filters
  `!node.id.contains(VIRTUAL_KEY_SEPARATOR)` over `snapshot.nodes()` (`graph.rs:171`). A node's `owner` comes from
  `select_of` (a select for its options), and its handlers and reads come from its element's facts; a node with no
  element fact gets none (`graph.rs:173-184`).
- **M2 — the actions listing follows the graph.** `actionable_nodes` lists a graph node whose `owner` is set,
  whatever the actionable rule reads, or one the rule holds for on its element (`actionable.rs:128-140`). `keyed` is
  `!node.id.contains('/')` (`actionable.rs:141-145`), so every `{owner}///{key}` id reads `keyed` false.
- **M3 — `actions` resolves a listed id through elements alone.** `Session::actions` maps each listed id through
  `element_ids()` (`actions.rs:59-73`). A listed virtual id finds no element, so every verb would read `stale`
  (`contract/actions-verb/stale`) unless the read gains a virtual arm.
- **M4 — one `not-found` arm serves five verbs.** `resolve` refuses any id holding `///` `not-found` at its head
  (`execute.rs:844-847`). Its callers are `type_into`, `scroll`, `screenshot`, `Session::layout` and
  `Session::canvas` (graph query, trace `tree-query-2026-11-25-virtual-nodes-in-every-read.json`). `resolve_click` is
  the one virtual arm (`execute.rs:860-876`).
- **M5 — the engine has no layout reason for a region.** `BaseDocument::layout_reason` takes an element's `NodeId` and
  answers none for anything else (`layout_reason.rs`; arch `contract/base-document/layout-reason`). `Placer::App
  { canvas }` is declared «Reserved: nothing places a node so yet» (`layout.rs:56-60`), is already written as `by:
  app` with a `canvas` key (`json/layout.rs:119`), and `layout`'s help already names «app for an element the app
  places inside a canvas» (`schema.rs:596-599`). The closed size causes are eleven, `layout` the catch-all «any box
  no earlier rule matches» (`layout_reason.rs:190-215`).
- **M6 — the reached record holds element ids.** `ReachedRecord::resolve` keys on the dispatch chain's elements and
  their current listeners (`reached.rs:111-128`). A click on a region is synthesized on the canvas element
  (`decision/custom-widget-click-synthesis`), so the canvas's id is recorded, never a virtual id. The fixture canvas
  carries no Dioxus listener; its widget handles the click itself (`fixtures/mod.rs:405-410`). Circle Drawer's canvas

**Change:** ~ decision/ui-graph-one-node-per-snapshot-node · rule: was «The read-only UI graph holds one node per snapshot node but a canvas's virtual nodes, which it excepts, so the actions answer and exploration hold none of them; names and closed words only.»; now «The read-only UI graph holds one node per snapshot node, a canvas's virtual nodes among them, each owned by its canvas with no handlers or reads, so the actions answer and exploration hold them too; names and closed words only.»
**Why:** decision/ui-graph-one-node-per-snapshot-node: The graph no longer excepts a canvas's virtual nodes, and the actions answer and exploration now hold them; handler coverage lists none, a virtual node carrying no handler, so the row names it nowhere. — on relayed verbatim by overseer1 and the escher overseer, 2026-11-25, inputs#I2: «A — id во всех чтениях записи (Recommended)»
**Ref:** .andromeda/runs/2026-11-25T13-41-29-wrap/

- Disabled-ness is keyed one way since 2026-10-13-stand-keyboard-harness (in every document, ratified by the founder): the `DISABLED` state (`:disabled`) reads the attribute's presence, and the pointer-move gate, `ClickTarget::Disabled`, `handle_click`'s walk gate, the Enter and Space activation and focusability read `ElementData::is_disabled` — that presence on a `button`, `input`, `select` or `textarea` alone (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18) — so `disabled="false"` and a bare `disabled` on a form control match `:disabled` and are not focusable, a bare `disabled` set after creation takes its focusability away, and a `<div disabled tabindex=0>` takes focus. dioxus-native-dom removes a falsy value of its 28 boolean attributes — upstream's `is_bool_attr` predicate since 2026-10-13-upstream-sync-polish-and-ship (`disabled`, `checked`, `hidden`, `inert` among them; a framework-written `inert: false` is removed, while a truthy `inert` (by presence on itself or an ancestor element) takes focusability, hits and the tree away from its subtree (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18) and Tab reaches the buttons under `inert: false`; HTML's focus fixup is built, in every document, so a node holding focus when it comes under `inert`, a subtree moved under an inert box included, gives focus up as the mutator flushes, no DOM `blur` or `focusout` firing; and a focused node that no longer shows gives focus up after each layout, no DOM `blur` or `focusout` firing, while a `display: contents` control and one beside a hidden sibling keep focus (ratified, the Tab walk's skip of unshown nodes remedying the Tab trap the post-layout fixup alone made; a control whose own `:focus-within` rule hides its container still takes Tab and loses focus at the next layout, a stated limit)), so a `hidden: false` element stays displayed, in the tree and in the snapshot; an attribute outside the list holding `false` is still written as `"false"`. The snapshot reads `enabled` by presence (on a virtual node the declaration's disabled flag, `enabled` false where declared disabled) — the driver's `disabled` refusal cause is stated on the same presence reading ("the element carries the `disabled` attribute, which the snapshot reads as not enabled") and is detected on it and on nothing else: the driver refuses a `click` or a `type` as `disabled` when the snapshot reads the element not enabled, with nothing dispatched and focus as it was, and acts on the same control once it reads enabled (`stand_act_disabled.rs`), and the driver's schema defines no role or name set of its own — `checked` a native checkbox's or radio's state, else, on a checkable role, the node's `toggled` reading (`True` true, `False` and `Mixed` false; ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18), and `value` from the element (a `select`'s `value` `BaseDocument::select_value` — the chosen option's value, for a `multiple` select its first chosen option's in tree order, nothing with none chosen — its options, its children and those under an `optgroup`, kept in the tree as `ListBoxOption` nodes, each `selected` from its chosen state, a closed drop-down's options under it with its select's client rect as their `bounds`, which the driver's visual lint leaves out of its overlap reading in every document with an open list's rows and groups, an open list's row reading its painted row's `bounds` (`Entry.in_select_box`, read through `closed_select_of` for a closed select's option and through `select_list_bounds` for an open list's row or group, never the role) — the stand's flight booker at boot no `overlap`, `stand_lint` reading `[0, 0, 0, 0]` — while a list box's rows and groups, `multiple` or of display size above 1, read their own client rects and its rows are linted as usual; a range input's `value` its current value since 2026-10-13-range-input-interaction — `ElementData::range_input_value`, the formatted value a key or a pointerdown moved, while its `value` attribute keeps the boot value; a password input's value reads the fixed mask `MASKED_VALUE` where it holds text and `""` where it holds none, a file input's where its `value` attribute is non-empty — and, since 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot, a password's typed text is in no painted frame either: blitz-paint paints its value as bullets, its caret at the bullet of its caret index, in every document and through every renderer that paints with blitz-paint, windowed included (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-12), two values of one length painting byte-identical frames, focused or not, in both layout modes (`password_painted_masked.rs`); a click inside a field holding a value places the caret by the bullets — `click_password_input` lays out one U+2022 per character through `BaseDocument::layout_as_text_input`, finds the bullet under the point and moves the real editor to that character, so no width of the real characters reaches the caret: two values of one length read one index, in both layout modes (`password_caret_click.rs`; ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18); the windowed paint is not run; a textarea's typed text reads back as its `value`, proven on an in-file fixture where it is named by `aria-label`), and `focused` from the tree, and `clickable` (a `bool` after `focused`, true where the vdom walk's current listeners hold `click` and the element is no disabled form control; `Snapshot::to_text` writes the token `clickable` after `focused` only when true, and `Snapshot::diff` reads it as `Reading::Clickable`) — focus proven after a click, a Tab press and Shift+Tab (`stand_snapshot_state.rs`). The snapshot's text form (`Snapshot::to_text`) reads that model, never the tree or a control: one line per node, its role and name the node's, with no second mapping (`stand_snapshot_text.rs`). The text's parts (`Snapshot::text_parts`, `TextPart`) are one more reader of that model through the text form and of nothing else — consecutive pre-order lines of `to_text`, never a split line, the parts concatenating to the whole text with every node id on exactly one line — and the driver's `snapshot` reads a screen over `SNAPSHOT_TEXT_BUDGET` in parts: on an over-budget fixture, in both layout modes, each part's lines equal their lines in the whole text, a password's line reads `MASKED_VALUE` in every part, and exactly one line reads `focused` after a click (`stand_snapshot_parts.rs`). The snapshot's diff (`Snapshot::diff`) is one more reader of that model: a text change is reported on the element whose accessible name it changes, by its id and never as a text-run entry, a hidden element leaves and returns with its descendants, and a focus move names exactly the controls whose `focused` reading moved (`stand_diff.rs`). Since 2026-10-10-mcp-surface an MCP tool result is one more reader of that model and of nothing else — a `snapshot` result is `to_text`'s output itself for a whole screen, equal byte for byte to `Session::run`'s screen text in both layout modes (`stand_mcp_tools.rs`), and, for a screen read in parts, its JSON line `{"text","part","parts"}` holding that part's text — through `serve_mcp` a walk's text blocks equal the JSON lines `Session::run` writes, in both layout modes (`stand_snapshot_parts.rs`), its crossing to an MCP client ratified by the founder (2026-10-10). Since 2026-10-12-self-description a password input typed through an MCP `type` reads `MASKED_VALUE` in the tool result, role `PasswordInput` and a non-empty name, the typed text in neither result, in both layout modes — a test-only element of the shared password page `fixtures::password_named` (`tests/blitz-tests/tests/fixtures/mod.rs`), no stand task or app gaining one; and two further readers of the same model state closed words only: the node keys' help that `help` serves (each key's reading, the boolean model's two limits among them) and `DiffNode::differs`, a changed node naming the readings that differ from before the step in node-key order — the Flight Booker's Book names eight nodes — seven that only moved, each `differs` = `[bounds]`, and since 2026-10-13-stand-keyboard-harness `flight-book` itself, which the click now focuses, `differs` = `[focused, bounds]` (`stand_diff.rs`). Since 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot the driver's `screenshot` is one more reader of the model's bounds and of nothing else in it — an element shot, addressed by stable id and refused as every id-addressed call is, is the node's bounds rounded outward and cropped to the part that can be seen — and a shot changes nothing: no focus moves, `has_changes` stays false and the next diff is empty, in both layout modes (`stand_act_screenshot.rs`). The canvas read, which reads one canvas element's draw commands (Circle Drawer's circles and diameter labels leaving only as shot pixels, as the canvas verb's draw commands and as the lint's truncated boxes, no label's text among them), and the virtual-node read, which reads one canvas's declared nodes, are no readers of the snapshot model; a canvas's virtual nodes are served by the reserved id form `{owner}///{key}` in the accessibility tree and, from it, the snapshot and its diff, the UI graph, the actions answer and the layout answer, these three never carrying the node's declared name, no element's id holding `///`.
